items.message: Operator-supplied `allow` strings and provider endpoint strings pass through `manifest()` without validation and are emitted verbatim to stdout via `egress-manifest`. If an endpoint registered in the provider registry or an `allow=` entry contains whitespace, shell metacharacters, or ANSI escape sequences, those reach the terminal or any script that consumes the manifest via command substitution. In `egress_manifest_cmd`, `_default_lockstep()` imports and evaluates the user's `lockstep.py` module, then `default_registry(Auth())` is called. Any exception from the registry is converted to a `ClickException` using `str(e)`, which may include credential material from an `AuthenticationError` or connection string embedded in the exception message. This is the same pattern as the rest of the CLI, so it is not new to this change — but the new command adds a new surface where `str(e)` from an au…[truncated]

The new JWT pattern `eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{4,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}` will match any string whose first segment starts with `eyJ`, which is the base64url encoding of `{"` — a very common prefix. The pattern is non-anchored and uses `re.search` semantics (inferred from the surrounding code). A base64-encoded value elsewhere in a log that happens to start with `eyJ` and contain two dots could be incorrectly redacted.
